}}
In March 2026, a state-commissioned environmental assessment report raised concerns about emissions of air pollutants exceeding regulatory thresholds of the [[Clean Air Act (United States)|Clean Air Act]], including [[carbon monoxide]] and [[particulate matter]] from vehicle use and continuously running generators.<ref>Green, Amy. (March 6, 2026). [https://insideclimatenews.org/news/06032026/florida-alligator-alcatraz-detention-site-pollution/ "Documents Raise New Concerns Over Alligator Alcatraz's Air and Climate Pollution"]. Inside Climate News.</ref> On May 26, 2026, the Center for Biological Diversity filed a lawsuit for what it terms as "substantial, unpermitted pollution from diesel generators and other air-polluting equipment", that could lead to civil penalties for Florida of up to $124,426 per day of violation. The air pollutants harm human health and the environment, including [[benzene]], [[formaldehyde]], [[NOx|nitrogen oxides]] and particulate matter.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.wgcu.org/section/immigration/2026-05-27/lawsuit-filed-over-alligator-alcatraz-air-pollution-cites-possible-extended-expected-shutdown-of-sites|title=Lawsuit filed over 'Alligator Alcatraz' air pollution, cites possible extended expected shutdown of site|author=Saunders, Jim; Kim, Dara Kam|publisher=[[WGCU (TV)|WGCU News]]|language=en-US|url-status=live|date=May 27, 2026|access-date=November 1, 2026|archive-date=June 10, 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260610013640/https://www.wgcu.org/section/immigration/2026-05-27/lawsuit-filed-over-alligator-alcatraz-air-pollution-cites-possible-extended-expected-shutdown-of-site}}</ref>

===Civil liberties challenges===
On July 16, 2025, the [[American Civil Liberties Union]], the ACLU of Florida, and Americans for Immigrant Justice filed a [[class action]] suit claiming the [[Second presidency of Donald Trump|Trump administration]] violates the [[First Amendment]] and [[Fifth Amendment to the United States Constitution|Fifth Amendment]] rights of people being detained, as well as the First Amendment rights of legal service organizations and law firms with clients held at the facility.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.wgcu.org/top-story/2025-07-16/class-action-lawsuit-filed-says-alcatraz-preventing-lawyer-access|title=Class-action lawsuit filed, says 'Alcatraz' preventing lawyer access|author=Saunders, Jim; Kim, Dara Kam|publisher=[[WGCU (TV)|WGCU News]]|language=en-US|url-status=live|date=July 16, 2025|access-date=November 1, 2026|archive-date=July 17, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250717191757/https://www.wgcu.org/top-story/2025-07-16/class-action-lawsuit-filed-says-alcatraz-preventing-lawyer-access}} - Retrieved August 30, 2025.</ref> The civil rights groups' lawsuit alleges detainees are [[Arbitrary arrest and detention|being held without charges and are not being given access to their attorneys]].<ref>(August 4, 2025) [https://www.npr.org/2025/08/04/1256727547/1a-08-04-2025 'If You Can Keep It': "Alligator Alcatraz" And Due Process.] [[NPR]]. Retrieved September 28, 2025.</ref> As part of this lawsuit that also contests the federal cancellation of bond hearings, [[U.S. District Judge]] [[Rodolfo Ruiz]] has requested all written agreements and contracts showing who has legal custody of the hundreds of detainees.<ref>Schneider, Mike (August 4, 2025) [https://thehill.com/policy/national-security/alligator-alcatraz-documents-florida/ "Judge orders Florida, federal officials to produce 'Alligator Alcatraz' agreements"] ''[[The Hill (newspaper)|The Hill]]''. Retrieved August 30, 2025.</ref>

Immigration attorneys described the facility's alternate system as a place "where the normal rules don't apply." Gov. Ron DeSantis falsely stated on July 25 that "Everybody here is already on a final removal order," a lie repeated by his director of emergency management, Kevin Guthrie.<ref name="auto5">Tony Pipitone (December 9, 2025, Updated on December 10, 2025 at 6:57 pm) [https://www.nbcmiami.com/news/local/secrets-of-alligator-alcatraz-revealed-in-newly-released-data-analyzed-by-nbc6-investigates/3732176/ Secrets of 'Alligator Alcatraz' revealed in newly released data analyzed by NBC6 Investigates]. [[NBC6 Miami]]. Retrieved January 8, 2026.</ref> Internal data show that the vast majority of detainees did not have final orders of removal from a judge before entering the facility (nearly 70% did not<ref name="auto5"/>), but they may have been deported as the facility's population fell to below 400 late August.<ref>Wieder, Ben and Dasgupta, Shirsho. (September 15, 2025) [https://www.miamiherald.com/news/local/immigration/article312042943.html "Hundreds of Alligator Alcatraz detainees drop off the grid after leaving site"] ''[[Miami Herald]]''. Retrieved 15 September 2025.</ref>

In January 2026, a former detainee from the camp deported to [[Colombia]] and a second who had requested asylum was deported to [[Haiti]] both testified before a District judge that the camp agents did not respect their right to legal counsel guaranteed by the [[Sixth Amendment to the United States Constitution]].<ref>Salomon, Gisele & Schneider, Mike. (January 29, 2026) [https://www.military.com/daily-news/2026/01/29/detainees-floridas-alligator-alcatraz-say-they-were-punished-seeking-legal-help.html "Detainees at Florida's 'Alligator Alcatraz' Say They Were Punished for Seeking Legal Help"]  ''Military News''.</ref> In April, lawyer Katherine Blankenship accused state and federal officials of failing to comply with a federal judge's preliminary injunction allowing detainees to phone their lawyer. Blankenship also declared that camp guards severely beat and [[pepper spray|pepper-sprayed]] detainees.<ref>CBS Florida Team. (April 15, 2026). [https://www.cbsnews.com/miami/news/florida-alligator-alcatraz-guards-beat-detainees-lawyer-claims/ Detainees at Florida's Alligator Alcatraz severely beaten by guards, pepper-sprayed, lawyer claims.] [[CBS News]].</ref>

== Public response ==
Critics compare the facility to [[Nazi concentration camps]], referring to it as "Alligator [[Auschwitz]]"<ref>{{Cite news |last=Walsh |first=Joan |date=2025-06-30 |title=The Abominable Sadism of "Alligator Auschwitz" |url=https://www.thenation.com/article/politics/sadism-alligator-auschwitz/ |access-date=2025-07-02 |language=en-US |issn=0027-8378 |archive-date=July 2, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250702184438/https://www.thenation.com/article/politics/sadism-alligator-auschwitz/ |url-status=live }}</ref> while others situate it within American concentration camps, including the [[internment of German Americans]], the [[internment of Italian Americans]], and the [[internment of Japanese Americans]]<ref>{{cite magazine |last1=Grant |first1=Melissa |title=The Grand Opening of an American Concentration Camp |url=https://newrepublic.com/article/197508/alligator-alcatraz-trump-concentration-camp |access-date=2 July 2025|magazine=[[The New Republic]]}}</ref> at [[Manzanar]] and elsewhere. Members of the [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican Party]], including DeSantis,<ref>{{Cite web|date=2025-07-01|first=Kathryn|last=Watson|title=Trump tours 'Alligator Alcatraz' immigration detention center in Florida|url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/trump-alligator-alcatraz-detention-center-florida/|access-date=2025-08-06|publisher=[[CBS News]]|language=en-US}}</ref> have defended the facility, arguing it will help the [[U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement]] (ICE) to cope with [[Deportation in the second presidency of Donald Trump|the deportation policy]] of [[Federal government of the United States|the federal government]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-06-29 |first=Bill |last=Hutchinson|title=Florida AG proposes 'Alligator Alcatraz' migrant detention center in Everglades |url=https://abc7.com/post/what-is-alligator-alcatraz-florida-ag-james-uthmeier-proposes-migrant-detention-center-everglades/16848113/|access-date=2025-08-06|publisher=[[ABC7 Los Angeles]]|language=en-US}}</ref> The camp has been labeled a "[[black hole]]" following the irregular disappearance of detainees.<ref>Fernández, Abel (18 September 2025) [https://english.elpais.com/usa/2025-09-18/the-mysterious-disappearance-of-hundreds-of-immigrants-detained-at-alligator-alcatraz.html The mysterious disappearance of hundreds of immigrants detained at Alligator Alcatraz]. ''EL PAÍS USA Edition.''</ref> [[Alex Padilla]], [[Dick Durbin]] and other Democratic U.S. Senators mentioned the camp in their open letter about the increase in deaths during ICE detention.<ref>Durbin, Dicke et al. (February 17, 2026) [https://www.padilla.senate.gov/newsroom/press-releases/padilla-durbin-senate-democrats-sound-alarm-on-dramatic-increase-in-deaths-in-immigration-detention/ Padilla, Durbin, Senate Democrats Sound Alarm on Dramatic Increase in Deaths in Immigration Detention] Press Release.</ref>

At a weekly vigil at the camp entrance on September 21, Amy Fischer, Director of Refugee and Migrant Rights at [[Amnesty International]] USA, called the facility "a human rights disaster."<ref>Bustos, R. Sergio. (September 21, 2025) [https://www.wlrn.org/immigration/2025-09-21/amnesty-international-usa-hold-vigil-to-call-for-alligator-alcatraz-closure "Religious leaders, Amnesty International USA hold vigil to call for Alligator Alcatraz's closure"], [[WLRN-TV|WLRN]]. Retrieved October 4, 2025.</ref> The organization launched a campaign to shut down the site on July 23 in response to unsanitary conditions, lack of medical care, and minimal access to lawyers, considering that it "sets a dangerous precedent for how states can partner with the federal government to expand the reach of its mass detention and deportation machine."<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.amnesty.org.uk/urgent-actions/shut-down-alligator-alcatraz |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251008193508/https://www.amnesty.org.uk/urgent-actions/shut-down-alligator-alcatraz |archive-date=2025-10-08 |title=USA: Shut down "alligator alcatraz" |access-date=October 4, 2025}}</ref> "Amnesty International considers that detention conditions at both facilities amount to cruel, inhuman and degrading treatment. The use of prolonged solitary confinement at Krome and the use of the [[box (torture)|'box']] at "Alligator Alcatraz" amount to torture or other ill-treatment."<ref name="auto3"/>

==Political responses==
After the facility's announcement, the [[Republican Party of Florida]] marketed "Alligator Alcatraz" merchandise, including hats, shirts, and koozies, the state of Florida handed out merchandise to conservative influencers, and Attorney General James Uthmeier sold similar items to raise election cash.<ref name="Ceballos 07012025"/> Critics found the fundraising pitch cruel and inaccurate as hundreds of people being held there are not facing any criminal charges and the facility could be described as a [[concentration camp]].<ref>Bendery, Jennifer (July 14, 2015). [https://www.huffpost.com/entry/nrcc-alligator-alcatraz-shirts-immigrants-mauled_n_686ff591e4b0d01c494d0d8f "House GOP Raises Money By Joking About Immigrants Being Mauled By Alligators"] ''HuffPost''. Retrieved August 9, 2025.</ref> Florida state Representative [[Angela Nixon]] called it a "modern-day concentration camp", explaining, “Donald Trump‘s blueprint for America has now become barbed wire and broken families.”<ref>Fields, Ashleigh. (July 2, 2025) [https://thehill.com/homenews/state-watch/5381970-angela-dixon-donald-trump-florida-alligator-alcatraz/ Florida state rep: Trump building ‘modern-day concentration camps’] ''[[The Hill (newspaper)|The Hill]]''.</ref>

On July 2, [[Janelle Bynum]], [[Maxwell Alejandro Frost]] and 22 other members of Congress wrote to Noem deploring that "detainees will be kept in tents with inadequate sanitation facilities and will face unbearable living conditions," including "exposure to deadly pathogens, constant threats from unpredictable flooding and extreme weather events, and daily temperatures averaging 90 degrees, with a heat index often over 100 degrees Fahrenheit."<ref>McCoy, Robert. (July 2, 2025) [https://newrepublic.com/post/197552/trump-alligator-alcatraz-flood Trump's "Alligator Alcatraz" Is Already Flooding] ''[[The New Republic]]''. Retrieved September 7, 2025.</ref>

In July, [[Florida House of Representatives|state Representative]] [[Anna Eskamani]] and [[Florida State Senate|state Senator]] [[Shevrin Jones]] joined lawmakers in suing DeSantis in order to gain access to the site. After their visit, they deplored the sanitary conditions, with Eskamani stating that the detention camp is "a political stunt with environmental damage and everyday lives being harmed. It needs to close immediately."<ref>Morel, Laura C. (July 22, 2025) [https://www.motherjones.com/politics/2025/07/alligator-alcatraz-the-mosquitoes-are-getting-worse-life-inside-floridas-secretive-everglades-detention-camp/ "'The Mosquitoes Are Getting Worse': Life Inside Florida's Alligator Alcatraz Detention Camp"] ''[[Mother Jones (magazine)|Mother Jones]]''.</ref>

Following an on-site visit on July 12, Representative [[Debbie Wasserman Schultz]] described the detainees as "essentially packed into cages, wall-to-wall humans, 32 detainees per cage". During the same visit, Florida Rep. [[aría Elvira Salazar]], who was able to enter a cage, said the center meets the "highest of standards".<ref>{{Cite news|last=Penley|first=Taylor|date=July 12, 2025|title=Republican lawmaker challenges Democrats' characterization of 'Alligator Alcatraz' after touring facility|publisher=[[Fox News]]|url=https://www.foxnews.com/media/republican-lawmaker-challenges-democrats-characterization-alligator-alcatraz-after-touring-facility}}</ref> Congressional and state lawmakers on-site reportedly heard cries of ''libertad'', meaning "freedom" in Spanish, from detainees. Lawmakers were not permitted to view the entire facility.<ref>{{Cite news|last1=Elassar|first1=Alaa|last2=Romo|first2=Rafael|date=July 12, 2025|title=Florida lawmakers allowed into 'Alligator Alcatraz' say detainees packed into cages|publisher=[[CNN]]|url=https://www.cnn.com/2025/07/12/us/alligator-alcatraz-lawmaker-tour-conditions|access-date=August 29, 2025}}</ref>

Representative [[Dan Goldman]] of [[ICE and New York City during the second Trump presidency|New York, where ICE is a contentious topic]], aided in the release of some 30 people on May 6, 2026, including at least one detained in the Everglades, stating, "our immigration system is being weaponized against those simply trying to follow the rules" and that he will "continue to use every tool in Congress to fight back and push for true accountability and reform."<ref>Sprayregan, Molly. (May 6, 2026) "[https://www.lgbtqnation.com/2026/05/gay-immigrant-reunited-with-husband-after-150-days-in-ice-custody-love-has-brought-him-home/ Gay immigrant reunited with husband after 150 days in ICE custody: "Love has brought him home]" ''[[LGBTQ Nation]]''.</ref>

=== Public opinion ===
Polling on July 4, 2025, by [[YouGov]] found that 48% of Americans polled opposed the detention center, with 33% supporting it and 18% unsure, while 53% of independents polled opposed the facility.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-07-04 |first=Joe |last=Sommerlad|title=Almost half of Americans disapprove of Florida's 'Alligator Alcatraz', new poll shows |url=https://www.the-independent.com/news/world/americas/us-politics/alligator-alcatraz-migrants-trump-poll-b2782882.html|access-date=2025-07-13|newspaper=[[The Independent]]|language=en-GB}}</ref> In their poll on July 20, 28% of women and 42% of men approved the camp.<ref>{{cite web|last=Gancarski|first=A. G.|date=July 15, 2025|title=Poll: 'Alligator Alcatraz' scores with Republicans, riles independents and Dems|url=https://floridapolitics.com/archives/747452-poll-alligator-alcatraz-scores-with-republicans-riles-independents-and-dems/|website=Florida Politics|access-date=July 20, 2025}}</ref> A poll among Florida voters from July 25 to 27 found that 34% of Floridians held a favorable opinion and 59% saying they disapprove of using the state of Florida's taxpayer-funded Emergency Preparedness and Response Fund to cover costs.<ref>The Florida Communications and Research Hub (July 30, 2025). [https://floridawatch.org/new-poll-floridians-unfavorable-to-alligator-alcatraz-concerned-about-taxpayer-cost/ NEW POLL: Floridians Unfavorable to 'Alligator Alcatraz,' Concerned About Taxpayer Cost]. Retrieved 6 September 2025.</ref>
